claims.text: The target system is single-crystalline CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy nanopillars tested at room temperature.
Chemical compositional fluctuations in CoCrFeNi nanopillars produce spatial variations in the generalized stacking-fault-energy landscape.
Rapid solidification can deliberately introduce controlled compositional fluctuations into the CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
Conventional processing produces chemically homogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillars with a uniform stacking-fault-energy distribution.
Spatially varying stacking-fault energies facilitate the joint or sequential activation of dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
Coordination of deformation twinning and dislocation slip promotes deformation delocalization.
Coordination of deformation twinning and dislocation slip delays necking failure.
Engineered compositional fluctuations will increase yield strength relative to a homogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillar baseline.
Engineered compositional fluctuations will increase uniform elongation relative to a homogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillar baseline.
CoCrFeNi nanopillars containing atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity can attain uniform elongation above approximately 100% at high flow stress under room-temperature tensile loading.
A homogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillar baseline exhibits lower yield strength than the proposed heterogeneous material.
A homogeneous CoCrFeNi nanopillar baseline exhibits lower ductility than the proposed heterogeneous material.
The proposed mechanism should hold under room-temperature tensile loading of nanoscale single-crystalline CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
The mechanism may not apply at elevated temperatures.
The mechanism may not govern behavior when other microstructural factors dominate.
Local stacking-fault-energy variations are difficult to quantify precisely.
Rapid-solidification processing may introduce microstructural changes other than compositional fluctuations, creating a confounding variable.

The mechanism is falsified if heterogeneous pillars fail to show statistically significant improvements in both yield strength and ductility or if SFE variation does not correlate with activation of both slip and twinning.
